programme.title: Planet Earth III
programme.desc: The third part of the nature documentary, produced over almost five years, concludes the trilogy almost two decades after the first series was broadcast.Its creators used pioneering film technologies, including:light drones, super-fast cameras and remotely controlled deep-sea submarines.In eight episodes, viewers will visit the most remote jungles, the darkest ocean depths, the world's largest caves and the hottest deserts and steppes.They will learn the story about nature's will to survive and the adaptive abilities of various species.The Earth is at a tipping point and changes in the natural world are felt in every ecosystem and affect numerous creatures.The series highlights the growing need to protect and restore nature.In the last episode, viewers will meet inspiring people from various corners of the world who are the face of change and saving the Earth.They are committed to risking their lives to protect the planet.Sir David Attenborough will guide the series.

programme.title: Life in Colour with David Attenborough
programme.desc: Traveler and naturalist David Attenborough will take viewers on a journey through the colorful world of nature.Discover the strategies of animals using colors for various purposes.Peacocks, baboons, tigers and chameleons use colors to attract attention or hide their presence and protect themselves and their loved ones.Animals found in various corners of the Earth use their own colors or those found in the environment to survive, attract a partner, convey information, scare away predators or protect their territory.The creators will use amazing shots and frames to show the beauty of the world around us, but also the cunning and strategies that animals use to survive.

programme.title: Attenborough's Wonder of Eggs
programme.desc: Bird eggs nurture new life, protecting it from the outside world while allowing it to breathe.They are strong enough not to break under the full weight of the incubating parent, and fragile enough for the chick to escape.From creation to hatching, Sir David Attenborough reveals the rich process behind these natural wonders.Along the way, he shares stories about the eggs of a whole range of birds - from swans and their aquatic world, to the cliffs where the common guillemot lives and lays its eggs.

programme.title: Attenborough's Wonder of Song
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough selects seven of the most extraordinary recordings from the natural world and explores what these sounds mean to specific animal species.Each song - from that of a lemur, through the song of a humpback whale or a lyrebird from the order of passerine birds - was recorded during the lifetime of a famous naturalist who recorded and analyzed these songs for decades.The oldest recording was made when Sir David was five years old, the latest just a few years before the documentary was created.Each has an amazing story behind it and shows how much we still don't know about the natural world.When Sir David Attenborough was born, the science of song was transformed under Charles Darwin's theory of sexual selection, which labeled singing dangerous because it revealed the singer's location to predators.The same singing also gives males a great chance to be noticed by the female, and thus to pass on their genes to the next bird generation.So the males sing, and the females listen and choose the best singers because, according to them, they will be the best fathers.New scientific trends in bird song are challenging these long-held ideas.Scientists invited to the program show that in fact, in most species of songbirds, females create their own songs - and only now do they have a chance to be truly heard.However, there is a concern as to whether we will be able to learn all the songs of these extraordinary birds - the human loss is loud and the planet Earth is falling silently, as the host of the program also warns.The production is a continuation of the Grierson Award-nominated documentary "The Egg: A Miracle of Nature".

programme.title: Attenborough's Birds of Paradise
programme.desc: David Attenborough presents his own perspective on the scientific discoveries, facts and myths surrounding the birds of paradise.He spent half his life filming and researching their habits both in the depths of the forest and in museums and nature collections in Europe.It tells the story of the fascination these birds arouse in the hearts of various people.Viewers will also learn what science says about them and their unusual behavior.In the final part of the program, David will take viewers to Qatar, where the world's largest breeding of birds of paradise has been established in a state-of-the-art facility.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Jurassic Sea Monster
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough accompanies a team of scientists to observe a skeleton found in Dorset.Together they examine the skull of a huge pliosaur.The reptile was named the marine tyrannosaurus.

programme.title: Exploration Volcano
programme.desc: Chris Horsley specializes in volcano exploration.In the program, he brings documentarians from around the world to volcanic trails to show them the effects of eruptions, which can wreak havoc and threaten communities.Chris's great expedition spans a wide range - from the jungles of the Congo to the lava-burnt cities of the Canary Islands, from the distinctive glacial plains of Iceland to the smoking archipelagos of Italy.In each episode, his team must face unique and unpredictable terrain.However, the team does not stop at anything.He wants to complete each mission, whether it's collecting molten lava straight from the source or installing state-of-the-art volcano monitoring systems.These activities are necessary to better understand the functioning of ruthless natural giants.

programme.title: Blue Planet 2
programme.desc: More than seven years have passed since the premiere of the second season of the nature super-production, but it still impresses with its great implementation.Its creators completed 125 expeditions in 39 countries over four years.They spent over six thousand hours diving in the depths and filming the coasts.The best scenes were selected from this spectacular material, taking viewers to inaccessible worlds.Their guide is Sir David Attenborough, who claims that we know less about the depths of our own planet than about the surface of Mars.The inhabitants of the ocean's depths influence our lives because they shape the climate and produce about half of the oxygen necessary for the functioning of the planet.They are also home to numerous representatives of the fauna kingdom.The development of technology has allowed man to look into their world, which was previously inaccessible.Scientists are also constantly expanding their knowledge of animal behavior.The first episode of the program is a journey through the waters surrounding the Seychelles, New Zealand, Japan and the Arctic.Filmmakers captured, among others, dolphins surfing in the Red Sea.They tracked walruses resting on melting ice in the Arctic.They followed killer whales and humpback whales feasting on herring schools in Norway.
